en: The *Āgāmi-pratyaya-sūtra*,
translated by an unknown hand and appended to the Eastern Jin records:
The Venerable Mahāmaudgalyāyana was with the Buddha on Mount Gṛdhrakūṭa, wandering about.
By the banks of the Ganges River, he saw many hungry ghosts undergoing various different punishments for their karmic offenses.
Upon seeing the Venerable Maudgalyāyana, they all conceived a heart of reverence and came forward to inquire about the causes and conditions of their plight.
One ghost asked, "I am constantly afflicted by headaches; I do not know what sin has caused this?
Maudgalyāyana replied:

“When you were formerly a human being, you were unable to practice patience; you struck the heads of sentient beings with sticks. Now you receive this floral retribution, while the fruit awaits in hell.
One ghost asked, “I am constantly afflicted by the pain of sores; what sin has caused this?”
He replied:

"When you were a human being, you lacked a heart of compassion; you burned down mountains and forests and harmed living beings. Now you receive this 'flower retribution,' while the 'fruit' awaits you in hell."
A certain ghost asked, "My entire body is festering with sores, and it is unbearable; what sin has caused this?
He replied:
"When you were a human being, you delighted in boiling pigs and sheep; now you receive this as a 'flower-retribution,' while the actual fruit awaits in hell.
Another ghost asked, "I have no satiety in eating and can never be full; what sin has caused this?"
He replied, "When you were a human being, although you fed sentient beings, you constantly left them unsatisfied; now you receive this floral retribution, while the fruit awaits you in hell."
One ghost asked, "I am constantly suffering from headaches; though I treat them, they cannot be cured. What sin has caused this?
He replied:

"When you were a human being, you did not respect the Way and its Virtue, and moreover, you insulted and reviled them; now you receive this 'flower-retribution,' while the actual fruit awaits in hell.
Another ghost asked:
"I gave birth to sons and daughters, all of whom were handsome and lovely, yet they all died young. My grief never ceases; what sin has caused this?"

He replied: "When you were a human being, you saw your son kill living beings; you rejoiced in it and ate the meat. Because of the killing, his life was shortened; because of your rejoicing, you suffered bitter torment. Now you receive this 'flower-retribution,' while the 'fruit' awaits you in hell."
One ghost asked:
"I have one husband who keeps many wives; though it is my turn to stay the night, I am not admitted. What sin has caused this?"
He replied:
"When you were a human being, you did not respect your husband and committed adultery with immodesty; now you receive this 'flower-retribution,' while the 'fruit' awaits in hell."
One ghost asked, "I constantly suffer from headaches, yet my male organ is ulcerated and festering; what sin has caused this?
He replied:
"When you were a human being, you committed sexual misconduct in a pure place such as a stupa or temple; now you receive this as the 'flower reward,' while the 'fruit' awaits in hell.
A ghost asked:
"I have received this body, which is coarse, rough, and impure; by what sin was this caused?"
He replied:

"When you were a human being, you did not honor those with virtue and treated good people with contempt; instead, you threw sand and dirt upon śramaṇas. Now you receive this 'flower reward,' while the 'fruit' awaits you in hell."
One ghost asked, "I eat more than a *hú* [a measure of grain], yet I am always hungry; what sin has caused this?
He replied:

"When you were a human being, you originally acted as a bhikṣu; you sought goods for the Saṃgha but consumed them yourself. Now you receive this floral retribution, while the fruit awaits you in hell."
A certain ghost asked, "I have received this form with swollen feet and a goiter on my neck; what sin has caused this?
He replied:
"When you were a human being, you caused people and various animals to carry heavy burdens without compassion; now you receive this as a 'flower-retribution,' while the actual fruit awaits in hell.
A ghost asked, "I have received this body and constantly suffer from heat and thirst; what sin has caused this?"

He replied, "When you were a human being, you delighted in fishing and hunting; you would throw the fish you caught onto the sand and soil, causing them to die in agony. Now you receive this as the 'flower reward,' while the actual fruit awaits you in hell."
One ghost asked, "I have received this body, yet I am mad, deluded, and without wisdom; what sin has caused this?
He replied:
"When you were a human being, you gave wine as an offering to others; now you receive this 'flower-retribution,' while the 'fruit' awaits you in hell.
Another ghost asked:
"The sons I have borne all turn around and devour me; what sin has caused this?"
He replied, "When you were a human being, you did not cultivate filial piety or support your parents; now you receive this 'flower reward,' while the 'fruit' awaits in hell.
Another ghost asked:
"I always vomit after eating; what sin has caused this?

He replied, "When you were a human being, there was someone who asked for food after midday; you gave it to them while scolding and reviling them in anger. You now receive the 'flower-retribution' (the precursor), while the 'fruit-retribution' awaits in hell."
One ghost asked, "In this life, my wealth and resources have never been lacking, yet I take pleasure in wearing tattered clothes; what crime has caused this?
He replied:
"When you were a human being, although you enjoyed giving alms, you immediately regretted it after giving; now you receive this 'flower-retribution,' while the 'fruit' awaits in hell.
Another ghost asked:
"I have received this single form and constantly lean against alleyways; I have no fixed place to stay overnight. What sin has caused this?"
He replied:

"When you were a human being, when guests came to seek lodging, you did not provide them with peace and security; seeing their conduct, you further reviled them in anger. Now you receive this 'flower-retribution,' while the actual fruit awaits in hell."
A certain ghost asked, "I have obtained this form, being neither male nor female; what sin has caused this?
He replied:
"When you were a human being, you lacked a heart of compassion and delighted in castrating six-footed livestock; now you receive this 'flower-retribution,' while the 'fruit' awaits in hell.
Another ghost asked, "I have received this body, yet I am lame and unable to walk; what sin has caused this?"

He replied, "When you were a human being, you delighted in practicing unrighteousness, binding men and animals so that they could not move about; now you receive this as the 'flower-retribution,' while the actual fruit awaits in hell."
A certain ghost asked:

"This body of mine is constantly afflicted by heat and thirst. While traveling, I saw the Ganges River, clear, cool, and beautiful; I entered it to bathe, hoping to obtain refreshing comfort to dispel my suffering from heat.

But as soon as I entered its waters, my entire body began to rot and decay. When I became thirsty and wished to drink, the moment a single mouthful entered my throat, my five viscera were scorched and ruined, and my flesh fell away from my bones."
"What offense has caused this?
He replied:

"When you were a human being, you delighted in acting as a physiognomist, judging the fortune or misfortune of others; your assessments were mostly false and rarely true. You would either disparage or praise people, claiming to possess special virtues to move their hearts and thereby seek profit and sustenance."
Furthermore, because they were deceitful and dishonest toward their parents, brothers, and kinsmen, they now receive this "flower-retribution.
The actual fruit of their actions lies in hell, where they undergo suffering a billionfold, beyond what can be fully described.
One ghost asked:

"Since I have been receiving this body, there has always been a fierce dog with a massive frame and sharp teeth, its two eyes blazing red. Day and night it constantly comes to devour my flesh; though my life-force is not yet exhausted, the flesh grows back immediately. I undergo this suffering again and again, with pain so unbearable that it cannot be endured. By what sin was this brought about?"
He replied:

"When you were a human being, you served as the master of a celestial shrine (*devāyatana*). Within that shrine, you took the blood of oxen and sheep to sacrifice to the gods, ate their flesh yourself, and said to the multitude:
'If you sacrifice to the gods, you will obtain great prosperity and good fortune!'"
"By committing various evil and heterodox acts to delude the common people, they now receive this 'flower-retribution,' while the actual fruit awaits them in hell.

Another ghost asked: "I have received this body and dwell constantly amidst impurity; my entire frame is smeared with filth, and whatever I eat is all unclean. I perpetually endure this suffering and cannot escape it; foulness and distress envelop my body, and my anxieties are beyond reckoning. By what sin was this brought about?"

He replied, “When you were a human being, you were a brahmin who did not believe in the Buddha-dharma; you took no pleasure in making offerings to śramaṇas or practitioners of the Way, and whenever they came to beg, you always wished to avoid seeing them.”
At that time, a practitioner of the Way came to beg from you.
You thought to yourself:
"I must employ some expedient means so that he does not come again."
He immediately took the bowl, filled it with excrement, and placed it at the bottom, covering it over with rice. He then brought it to the practitioner.

Having received it, the practitioner returned to his original place and set it down to one side. After washing his hands thoroughly, he sat down and took up the bowl; as he reached out his hand to eat, he found the contents of the bowl were impure and so foul-smelling that they could not be approached.

Because of these causes and conditions, they suffer this stench and affliction; now they receive the "flower retribution," while the "fruit" awaits in hell, where they constantly swallow hot iron balls, their bodies rot and decay, and their suffering is beyond description.
One ghost asked:
"I have received this body such that tongues emerge from every place; there is a natural axe that chops them off, and this happens countless times. What sin has caused this?"
He replied:

"When you were a human being, you were a young novice monk. You were appointed by the Sangha to fetch cool, pure water and prepare stone-melodious syrup (śarkarā-pānaka), which you then distributed among the assembly of monks."
The rock honey was hard and large; he broke off a small portion and stole a mouthful to eat.

Because he had stolen the property of the Sangha, he now undergoes this "flower retribution" (the present manifestation), while the "fruit retribution" (the ultimate consequence) awaits him in hell, where he must swallow molten copper—a suffering beyond description.
One ghost asked, "I have received this body and am constantly tormented by hunger.
When I go to the latrine, wishing to take excrement to eat, there is a powerful ghost at the latrine who strikes me with a staff so that I cannot even approach. What sin has caused this?"

He replied, "When you were a human being, you once served as a practitioner and was the steward of a Buddhist monastery (*stūpa*). You were stingy in guarding the property of the Sangha; you did not provide the community of monks with fine food, but constantly gave them coarse and poor-quality fare."
At times, when he wished to prepare fine food, if a visiting bhikṣu arrived, he would stop and not cook, waiting until the guest had left before providing it.
Because of his evil mind of stinginess and parsimony, he now receives this "flower-retribution," while the "fruit" awaits him in hell.
One ghost asked, "I have received this body;
my belly is as large as a jar, yet the rest of my limbs are all small, and my throat is like the eye of a fine needle. I cannot swallow food. What sin has caused this?"
He replied:

"When you were a human being, you served as the head of a village. Relying on your own power and influence, you oppressed the people and constantly extorted food and drink from them through unrighteous means, bringing suffering upon the common folk. Now you receive this 'flower-retribution,' while the 'fruit' awaits you in hell."
A certain ghost asked:

"I have received this body, with a copper jar upon my shoulder filled with molten copper. With my hand I grasp a ladle to scoop it up and pour it over my own head; my entire body is scorched and seared. This has happened countless times, and my suffering is immeasurable. What sin has caused this?"
He replied:

"When you were a human being, you left the household life to practice the Way and served as the overseer of the Sangha's food and drink. You hid a jar of ghee elsewhere; when visiting monks arrived, you did not give it to them, but once they had departed, you brought out the ghee and distributed it to the resident monks."

This ghee is the property of the Saṃgha of the four quarters; all have a share in it. By concealing the property of the Saṃgha and giving it away unfairly, one incurs such suffering through these causes and conditions.
Having now received this as the "flower-retribution," the "fruit" awaits in hell, where the suffering endured will be beyond calculation.
One ghost asked:

"Having received this body, people constantly come with various knives and saws to cut and flay my flesh; they further split open my belly and pull out my five viscera. My flesh is exhausted and my tendons severed, and the pain is unbearable."
In the space of a moment, the flesh grew back as it was before; he then came again to cut it off. "By what sin has this been brought about? they asked.

He replied, "When you were human beings, you were brahmins who did not believe in the True Dharma and constantly gave rise to wrong views. You served celestial deities and perpetually offered prayers with cattle and sheep. Because of these sins, you now receive this 'flower-retribution,' while the 'fruit' awaits you in hell."
One ghost asked:

"Having received this body, people constantly come with various knives and saws to cut and flay my flesh; they further break open my belly and pull out my five internal organs. My flesh is exhausted and my tendons severed; the agony is so acute that it is unbearable."
In an instant, the flesh grew back as it was before; he then came again to cut it off. "By what sin has this been brought about?

[The man] replied, "When you were a human being, you constantly served as an executioner, presiding over the killing of men with no heart of compassion, performing these acts with joy. Because of such sins, you have incurred this misfortune; you now receive this 'flower-retribution,' while the 'fruit' awaits in hell."
One ghost asked:

"I have received this body, and beneath both my armpits there are constantly revolving wheels of hot iron; great heat oppresses my body and my two armpits are scorched and rotten. What sin has caused this?"
He replied:

"When you were a human being, you left home to study the Way and prepared various cakes for the Sangha. Before the monks had even begun to eat, you greedily stole some of the cakes, hid them under your armpit in a secluded spot, and ate them. Because of this cause and condition, you have incurred such suffering; now you receive the 'flower-retribution,' while the 'fruit' awaits in hell, where you shall undergo immeasurable agony."
One ghost asked:

"I have received this body, and there are always naturally occurring red iron balls that fall from the air into my mouth and reach my belly; sometimes they exit from the left and enter through the right, or exit from the right and enter through the left. My entire body is scorched and烂 (withered/rotten), and the pain is immeasurably acute. By what sin was this caused?"
He replied:
"When you were a human being, you left the household life as a śrāmaṇera and cooked mangoes for the Saṃgha.
As the food was being distributed among the monks, whenever it reached the position of the Elder, you would invariably give him seven extra fruits."
"Because of these causes and conditions, you have incurred such evil; now you receive this as the 'flower-retribution,' while the 'fruit' awaits in hell.
Another ghost asked:

"I have received this body, and when I wish to move about or turn back, it is like a whirlwind that cannot advance at all. My grief, distress, and suffering are beyond measure; what sin has caused this?"
He replied:

"When you were a human being, you served as a diviner, deceiving others and causing their minds to be deluded; whether they felt joy or fear, it was all untrue. Due to these causes and conditions, you have incurred such evil; what you now experience is the 'flower-retribution,' while the 'fruit' awaits in hell."
One ghost asked:

"I have received this body, which is constantly hot within, as if harboring boiling water and fire; it further comes to burn and cook me, causing ten thousand kinds of suffering. What sin has caused this?"
He replied:
"When you were a human being, you were the principal consort of a king.
At that time, the king held his junior consort in high esteem and respect; you constantly harbored jealousy and devised wicked schemes, seeking to have her killed."
While he was sleeping, [the king] boiled ghee until it was hot and poured it over his belly.
That man suffered immeasurable agony from this and subsequently passed away.
Due to these causes and conditions, he experienced such suffering; now he receives the "flower-retribution," while the "fruit" awaits him in hell.
A certain ghost asked:

"I have received this body, and my nature is one of much terror; I am constantly afraid that people will come to arrest, confine, bind, or subject me to shackles and cruel torment. I never feel joy. What sin has caused this?"
He replied:

"When you were a human being, you delighted in committing sexual misconduct and violated other women; you were constantly afraid of being discovered and your mind was never at peace. Now you receive this 'flower-retribution,' while the 'fruit' awaits in hell—either lying upon an iron bed or embracing a copper pillar. Such sufferings are beyond calculation."

One ghost asked, "I received this body, which is naturally made of glowing iron and covered with a cage-like net that entangles my frame; it burns, sears, and rots me, its agonizing pain beyond words. What sin has caused this?"
He replied, "When you were a human being, you constantly held snares and nets to kill fish and beasts, and used cages to capture birds.
Because of these causes and conditions, you have incurred such bitter suffering; what you now experience is the 'flower-retribution,' while the actual fruit awaits in hell."
One ghost asked:

"I have received this body, yet I have no hands or feet; it is like a single piece of flesh lying in a wilderness where foxes, wolves, tigers, leopards, vultures, eagles, and various birds compete to peck and claw at it, struggling together to devour it. The pain is beyond description—by what sin was this brought about?"
He replied:
"When you were a human being, you employed evil means—whether against yourself or others—and as soon as a woman became pregnant, you gave her medicine to cause the fetus to be destroyed."
"By reason of these causes and conditions, you have incurred such suffering; now you receive the 'flower-retribution,' while the 'fruit' awaits you in hell.
Furthermore, three ghosts came at once and asked:

"We have received this body, and there are always iron nails falling from the sky, nailing our bodies, piercing our flesh and breaking our bones, with a painful venom that penetrates to the marrow. By what sin is this caused?"
He replied:
"When you were human beings, one of you was a horse trainer, another a cow trainer, and another an elephant trainer.

Out of greed for the wealth of others, you cruelly inflicted pain upon them with needles and prods; yet you did not alleviate their suffering. Due to these causes and conditions, you have obtained such suffering. What you are experiencing now is the 'flower reward' (the preliminary retribution), while the 'fruit' awaits in hell."
A certain ghost asked, "I have received this body, yet it has no head;
my eyes, ears, nose, and mouth are all located upon my chest. What sin has caused this?"
He replied,
“When you were a human being, if you saw someone being killed, you seized them by the head and pulled with joy, lacking any heart of compassion.”
"By reason of these causes and conditions, they have obtained such bodies; they now undergo the 'flower reward,' while the 'fruit' awaits them in hell.
After Maudgalyāyana had answered the hungry ghosts, they all gave rise to a heart of reverence and ran forward to repent.
Seeing that they were joyful, Maudgalyāyana preached the Dharma for them once more.
Upon hearing it, all the hungry ghosts were filled with great joy.
*The Scripture on the Retribution of Hungry Ghosts*.
